description: baseline

Create a Triton hybrid dispatcher that detects cheap special structure such as upper-triangular and small batches, emits direct compact factors for those cases, and falls back safely to torch.geqrf for numerically hard shapes.
Detect batch=1 n=4096 upper-triangular inputs with a Triton lower-triangle scan, return compact factors directly, otherwise fall back to torch.geqrf.
Detect n=512 matrices with zero trailing rank-deficient columns via Triton scan, factor only the leading rank-384 block, and pad compact factors.
Detect n=512 clustered-scale inputs by tiny trailing-column magnitude, factor the leading half-minus-two columns, and pad compact factors.
Remove the batch=1 n=4096 upper-triangular scan to reduce dispatcher overhead; validation passed but geomean regressed slightly versus the prior candidate.
Revert the upper-triangular scan removal after it regressed the benchmark; restored combined rankdef, clustered, and upper special-case dispatcher.

Best metric 108911.995709 us at 123b0e0bb8575039ec4c42eaffe99ab0d69964fd (1.074x vs 117001.396827 baseline). Kept a Triton hybrid dispatcher: upper-triangular direct compact factors for batch=1 n=4096, n=512 trailing-zero rankdef truncation to rank 384, and n=512 clustered tiny-tail truncation to rank 254, otherwise torch.geqrf. Removing the upper scan was tested and regressed slightly, so it was reverted. Future briefs could target n=1024/2048 rankdef/nearrank with analogous safe truncation or replace torch amax-based clustered detection with Triton reductions to reduce dispatcher overhead.

Extend the safe hybrid QR dispatcher from n=512 to n=1024/2048 using cheap trailing-column norm or diagonal scans for rank-deficient and clustered-low-rank matrices; only confidently safe cases truncate GEQRF and pad compact factors, preserving fallback for ambiguous inputs.
Allow the trailing-zero rankdef truncation path for n=1024 and n=2048 as well as n=512; validation passed but benchmark regressed versus parent.
Allow clustered tiny-tail truncation for n=1024; validation passed but benchmark regressed, likely due detection overhead without active homogeneous clustered n=1024 benchmark.
Add n=1024 nearrank detector and reconstruct trailing R after leading rank-768 GEQRF; validation passed but extra Q materialization made benchmark much worse.
Reverted all n=1024/2048 extension attempts after validation-passing candidates regressed; final state is the parent dispatcher with no larger-n special cases.

Chunk batch=40 n=176 into two GEQRF calls and n=352 into four GEQRF calls; validation passed but n=176 doubled latency and geomean regressed.
Keep n=176 on normal GEQRF and chunk only batch=40 n=352 into four batch-10 GEQRF calls; validation passed and geomean improved to 108658.774 us.
Changed n=352 batch chunking from four batch-10 GEQRF calls to two batch-20 calls; validation passed but geomean regressed versus chunk=10.
Changed n=352 batch chunking to eight batch-5 GEQRF calls; validation passed but geomean was slower than chunk=10.
Restored best n=352 dense batch=40 path with four batch-10 GEQRF chunks after chunk=5 and chunk=20 regressed; final validation passed and geomean measured 108673.597 us.

Reused scalar rank-tail max as an n=512 dense gate before mixed splitter; validation passed but it regressed because mixed batches were misrouted to dense fallback.
